title: macOS Desktop Portfolio
summary: A macOS-style desktop that opens this portfolio as draggable Finder, Terminal, Safari, and Resume windows above a magnifying dock.
technicalDescription: Native React client component with pointer-drag windows, z-index focus store, proximity-weighted hero type, and cursor-distance dock magnification; no backend, no new dependencies.

caseStudy.problem: Portfolio content usually lives behind scroll navigation. A desktop shell lets visitors open the same projects, writing, and contact paths as windows, folders, and dock apps.
ownership: Ported a Vite plus GSAP plus Zustand macOS desktop spec to native Next.js App Router idioms so the demo ships with zero new dependencies.
Built menu bar, hero, folders, draggable windows, and magnifying dock as one client component with embedded and fullscreen modes.
architecture: Single client component (components/MacOsDesktop.tsx) with CSS Module styling; window open, focus, and z-index state in React useState.
Window dragging via pointer events on title bars; dock magnification and hero variable-weight type via cursor-distance weighting with requestAnimationFrame-free inline updates.
Fullscreen route at /demos/macos-desktop inside DemoShell; embedded preview on this project page via MacOsDesktopInteractive.
decisions: Skipped zustand, immer, GSAP, react-pdf, react-tooltip, and dayjs from the source spec: React state plus pointer events plus native Date cover the same interactions without dependency churn on Next 15 and React 19.
Resume opens as an embedded PDF iframe with a download action instead of a react-pdf bundle.
verification: npm test passes; npm run build passes; /demos/macos-desktop opens, windows drag and focus, dock magnifies on hover.
Spot-checked /agent.json and /llms.txt for the new project and demo entries.
limitations: No minimized-to-dock restore animation yet; minimize hides the window and the dock badge marks it open.
Finder covers curated portfolio locations, not the full site file tree.
productionDifferences: A standalone Vite build of the original spec would code-split each window; here the shell ships as one route bundle on magro.dev.
